3. Facts relevant for disposal of the Rules are that the opposite party no.1 in Civil Revisions as plaintiffs instituted Other Class Suit Nos.1005 of 1983, 1006 of 1983 and 1004 of 1983 in the Court of Munsif, Naogaon, for declaration that the cancellation order dated' 11.07.1982 passed by the Sub-Divisional Officer, Naogaon in permanent. Settlement Case No. 18 of 1982 is illegal, void and not binding upon the plaintiffs contending inter alia that the suit land is khas land of the Government. Plaintiff prayed for permanent lease and after observing necessary formalities Government leased out the same to the plaintiffs and since then they are in possession of the suit land. On an application filed by the present petitioner Nos.1-5, Sub-Divisional Officer, Naogaon, cancelled the aforesaid settlement without hearing the plaintiffs. Hence, the present suit. 

 14. The leasing authority after proper verification leased out the suit land to the landless plaintiffs. Thereafter the plaintiffs mutated their names in the Khatian and also paid rent to the Government exchequer. It appears that in the Khas Khatian No.1 prepared in the name of Government of Bangladesh, represented by the Collector, Rajshahi, suit Plot No.2411 described as an agricultural land. From the local inspection report submitted by the Advocate Commissioner, Khas Khatian No.1 prepared in the name of the Government and also from the deposition of the P.Ws it is apparent that the suit land was once a river but by the passage of time the same is converted as agricultural land and as such the report submitted by the Magistrate without hearing the plaintiffs is not proper rather arbitrary. The Government also treated the same as cultivable land and on considering the true state of affairs the leasing authority leased out the same to the plaintiffs. The leasing authority cancelled the lease of the plaintiffs without giving them an opportunity of hearing which is violated of the principles of natural justice. The appellate court below after assessing the evidence on record independently arrived at a finding that it appears from the local inspection report of the learned Advocate that the suit land is an agricultural land at present and there is no water way or any way on the Suit land. The appellate court below is the last court of fact' and the High' Court in exercise of revisional jurisdiction under Section 115 of the Code of Civil Procedure shall not ordinarily interfere with the findings of fact recorded by the court below unless it appears to it that the court below patently committed illegality and took a wrong view of law, as a result of which it arrived at an erroneous findings of fact by illegal exercise of jurisdiction. 

 16. In the present case also the nature and character of the suit land has been changed and the Government also treated the same as cultivable land which is apparent from Khas Khatian No.1 prepared in the name of the Government and considering the true state of affairs the Government leased out the same to the plaintiffs earlier. But on an application filed by the present petitioners who are local persons and enemical to the plaintiffs the leasing authority cancelled the lease without hearing the plaintiffs which is arbitrary and violation of the principles of natural justice.
